children: By Chris Munro

Bamboo Insurance Services’ decision to postpone its initial public offering comes at a time of dislocation in financial markets, a more selective investor environment and concerns that softening insurance rates could lead to prolonged pressure on industry returns.
This publication reported in mid-September that Bamboo was targeting a valuation of $3 billion through an IPO.
The proposed offering comprised secondary shares to be sold by affiliates of CVC Capital Partners and White Mountains Insurance Group.

On September 14, Bamboo set a target price range of $18 to $20 for the offering of 35 million shares. At that price, the company would have raised up to $700 million with a valuation of more ​than $3 billion.
The Midvale, Utah-based company had applied to list on the New York Stock Exchange ​under the symbol BMB.
JP Morgan and Morgan Stanley were lead bookrunners, while Deutsche ​Bank Securities, Evercore ISI and Wells Fargo Securities were among the other underwriters.
According to sources, the homeowners-focused MGU was slated to go public on September 23, but Bloomberg reported the day before that Bamboo had postponed the move.
Bamboo declined to comment on the rationale behind its decision to pause the IPO.

However, sources said the decision was tied to market conditions, and that the company would continue to evaluate its options, with speculation Bamboo could potentially restart the process later this year.
MIXED IPO PERFORMANCE
The decision to halt the process follows a mixed bag for IPOs this year.
Of the 10 largest IPOs on US exchanges this year, just five companies ended trading on September 23 above their offer prices.
Those were SpaceX, SK Hynix, Cerebras Systems, Forgent Power Solutions and Braveheart Bio.
The five whose share prices closed below their offer price on September 23 were Quantinuum, Parabilis Medicines, Electra Therapeutics, EquipmentShare and Orion180 Insurance Group.
Orion180 was the first P&C company to go ⁠public in the US this year. Seven P&C insurance-related companies undertook IPOs in 2025.
ORION180 GOES PUBLIC

Technology-enabled Orion180's portfolio predominantly comprises E&S and admitted homeowners insurance, alongside a smaller private flood book. The company also offers a range of ancillary products through a network of over 14,000 active independent agents.
Orion180 has two in-house fronting carriers — Orion180 Insurance Company and Orion180 Select Insurance Company — that, respectively, provide E&S and admitted program capacity to its MGA unit.
The two fronting carriers seek ​to retain between 15% and 30% of insurance risk, with the rest ceded to various reinsurance partners.
Melbourne, Florida-based Orion180 started trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on September 18 after raising $240 million in an IPO.
However, Orion180’s IPO was priced at $12 a share, down from its $15 to $17 ​targeted range.
Shares in Orion180 ended their first day of trading at $11.77 and closed on September 23 at $9.75.

In an interview with sister title The Insurer shortly after Orion180 went public, the company’s CEO Ken Gregg described the IPO as “a milestone for us” that “positions us differently in the marketplace.”

During the interview, Gregg said he took a long-term view and was less focused on short-term volatility. And while Orion180 went public during a softening property market, Gregg said the company planned for disruption.

“That's what gives confidence that we're going to be there long term, and we'll continue growing regardless of the markets,” he said. “The companies that can't navigate different market cycles, that's an issue for them that we don’t have because we can find different opportunities.”
ACCELERANT TO BE TAKEN PRIVATE

Meanwhile, Accelerant has agreed to be taken private by software-focused investment firm ​Thoma Bravo in an all-cash deal valued at more than $4 billion, the Jeff Radke-led company announced in August.
The ‌deal offers Accelerant shareholders $20.25 per Class A or Class B share and represents a 49% premium to its closing price on August 12, but a discount to its $21 IPO price in July 2025.

Accelerant operates as a data-driven marketplace that serves MGAs. It currently has over 300 MGA members and more than 97 risk capital partners that together support more than 700 products, according to its website.
Thoma Bravo’s acquisition of Accelerant is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to shareholder and ‌insurance ⁠regulatory approvals.
A more positive outcome for a recent programs and MGA market IPO can be seen with Neptune Insurance Holdings.
The Trevor Burgess-led business priced its IPO of 18.4 million shares at $20 and listed on the New York Stock Exchange on October 1, 2025.
Since then, the flood specialist’s share price has fluctuated but rarely closed below its IPO price. On September 23, 2026, Neptune’s share price ended the day’s trading at $27.76.
